children: SanDisk Corp. (SNDK, Financials) The semiconductor business focused on NAND flash memory and storage solutions had its chief technology officer sell over $8 million of stock after a rapid surge.

Executive Vise President and CTO Alper Ilkbahar sold 5,132 shares on Sept. 3 for approximately $7.9 million. The most recent filing showed 400 shares sold for approximately $625,557, plus 4,732 shares disclosed separately.
A further 3,244 shares, worth roughly $5 million, were withheld to pay tax obligations on vesting. That deal was not an open market sale.
The timing is sure to raise eyebrows, given SanDisk shares have risen more than 2,000% in the past year. But there is a great difference.

The sales were made under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted June 4, meaning they were prearranged and not necessarily tied to the stock's recent move. Following the stated transactions, Ilkbahar holds directly 40,490 shares.

For investors, the transaction is less a sudden gloomy signal than a reminder of how far SanDisk's valuation has come. The next test is whether earnings and memory pricing can continue to justify expectations after the stock's phenomenal climb.

title: SanDisk's CTO Just Sold Nearly $8 Million After a Huge Stock Run
